title: The Next.js 9.5 RCE Came From libheif
caption:
I have never once looked at what next/image pulls in.

It pulls in sharp. sharp pulls in libheif. On Aug 25 a crafted AVIF through libheif became an unauthenticated 9.5 RCE in Next.js, and every release back to 10.0.0 was in range.

The fix is 15.5.24 or 16.3.3. The uncomfortable part is that no amount of reading my own code would have found it.

Read your lockfile lately?

slides.headline:
Your image tag
scored 9.5
slides.sub: GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4, Aug 25: a crafted AVIF through the Next.js image optimization API is unauthenticated remote code execution.

slides.title: It isn't Next.js
slides.sub: next/image hands AVIF decoding to sharp. sharp hands it to libheif. The bug is libheif's, rated 9.8 on its own advisory.

slides.headline:
Two bytes into
a one-byte slot
slides.sub: libheif accepts a duplicate alpha plane, allocates 8-bit storage, then casts to uint16_t* and writes 2 bytes per sample. Heap overflow, attacker-controlled. Fixed in 1.23.2.

slides.title: Check your lockfile
items: Second critical the same day: CVE-2026-75604, path traversal to RCE on Windows-hosted Next.js 13.4 through 16.3.2.
That one lists no known workaround. Upgrading is the fix.

slides.headline:
So they turned
AVIF off
slides.sub: From the advisory: "Until a fix has propagated, optimization of AVIF files is disabled." A whole image format switched off to close one dependency's hole.
